report.summary: Proposed delivery plan: 9 items from reviewed findings, prioritized by severity and dependency. Gate 0 fixes critical integrity-trust-gap and high-severity killswitch-force-bypass. Gate 1 addresses repo-state-mismatch, invisible-dependency-interface, cross-file-type-resolution-gap, silent-failure-propagation, git-subprocess-contract. Gate 2 handles duplicated-gitdir-pointer and closure-capture-ambiguity.
risks: Integrity fix may require adding crypto library, increasing complexity.
Repo state restore may be non-trivial if evaluate_change has side effects.
Cross-file resolution gap may be deep; adding index may require architectural change.
Silent failure fix may uncover latent bugs in callers.
Git contract fix may require changing return types, affecting multiple callers.
todos: Inspect evaluate_change in correctness.py to confirm current behavior.
Trace resolve_type_graph call chain to determine if imports_by_file index is provided.
Search for all callers of _ask in llm.py and check empty string handling.
Inspect all callers of _git in mint.py for None handling.
Compare the two _read_gitdir_pointer implementations for differences.
Search for additional assignments to 'disc' in bootstrap.py after line 602.

items.title: Add cryptographic verification for receipts loaded from disk in gate_discrimination
items.why_now: Without verification, receipts can be forged, compromising the integrity of the entire system. This is a critical security vulnerability.

steps.do: Modify gate_discrimination to call a verify_signature function on loaded receipts before use.
steps.verified_by: Run test_receipt_verification.py: assert that a tampered receipt raises an error.

steps.do: Add verify_signature function (or reuse existing crypto) and ensure it is called.
steps.verified_by: Unit test: verify_signature returns False for invalid signature.

items.assumption: A cryptographic signature scheme (e.g., Ed25519) is acceptable and keys are available.

items.title: Propagate OSError when unlink fails during arm(force=True)
items.why_now: Silently ignoring permission errors can leave the system in an inconsistent state where both marker and permit exist, breaking the killswitch guarantee.

steps.do: In arm.py, change the OSError handling in the unlink call to only ignore FileNotFoundError, re-raise other OSError.
steps.verified_by: Test: set marker file permissions to read-only, call arm(force=True), assert that an error is raised.

items.assumption: The marker file path is accessible and permissions can be set in test.

items.title: Ensure evaluate_change restores repository state after evaluation
items.why_now: If state is not restored, drift.scan's repo_state becomes stale, causing incorrect drift reports and potential data corruption.

steps.do: Inspect evaluate_change in correctness.py to see if it uses a context manager or explicit restore. If not, add restore logic.
steps.verified_by: Test: call evaluate_change, then check that git status matches original state.

items.assumption: The repository state can be captured and restored (e.g., via git stash or snapshot).

items.title: Document and test external dependencies in interface module
items.why_now: Undocumented dependencies (session, parse, etc.) can change silently, breaking consumers. This is a high-risk maintenance issue.

steps.do: Add docstrings to all public functions in interface.py describing expected inputs and outputs.
steps.verified_by: Code review: all functions have clear docstrings.

steps.do: Write interface tests that validate the behavior of live_egress_seats, check_import_provenance, etc.
steps.verified_by: Run pytest on test_interface_dependencies.py; all tests pass.

items.assumption: The dependencies are stable enough to test in isolation.

items.title: Ensure cross-file type resolution receives proper imports_by_file index
items.why_now: Without a complete index, cross-file type resolution is incomplete, leading to incorrect type analysis.

steps.do: Trace call to resolve_type_graph and verify that the imports_by_file index covers all files. If not, modify the caller to pass a complete index.
steps.verified_by: Test: call resolve_type_graph with a partial index and assert that cross-file types are not resolved; with full index, they are.

items.assumption: The index is built elsewhere (e.g., build_index) and can be made available.

items.title: Log exceptions in _ask and ensure callers handle empty string return
items.why_now: Silent failures in _ask can propagate undetected, causing downstream modules to malfunction. Logging and explicit error handling are needed.

steps.do: Modify _ask in llm.py to log caught exceptions before returning empty string.
steps.verified_by: Test: mock an exception in _ask, assert that it is logged.

steps.do: Check all callers of _ask and add empty string checks where missing.
steps.verified_by: Test: call _ask to return empty, assert that callers handle it (e.g., raise or fallback).

items.assumption: Logging is acceptable and callers can be modified.

items.title: Standardize git subprocess return type handling in mint.py
items.why_now: Inconsistent return types (None vs empty list) can cause crashes in callers that assume a sequence type on git failure.

steps.do: Inspect all callers of _git in mint.py and add None handling (e.g., 'result or []') where missing.
steps.verified_by: Test: mock _git to return None, assert callers handle it without crash.

items.title: Unify duplicated _read_gitdir_pointer implementations
items.why_now: Two implementations risk divergence, leading to incorrect admin dir resolution in one path.

steps.do: Compare both implementations and refactor so one calls the other, or create a shared helper.
steps.verified_by: Test: both functions return the same gitdir pointer for the same repo.

items.title: Refactor closure to avoid capture ambiguity in bootstrap.py
items.why_now: Low risk, but future changes could introduce a bug if a third assignment to disc is added.

steps.do: Refactor _finish to take disc as an explicit parameter instead of capturing it from the closure.
steps.verified_by: Test: existing behavior remains unchanged; no capture of disc variable.

items.assumption: The refactoring does not break other uses of _finish.
